The present invention relates to [1] a colored fine particle dispersion containing colored fine particles and a neutralizing agent, in which the colored fine particles are produced by subjecting a monomer mixture containing an acid group-containing polymerizable monomer to emulsion polymerization in the presence of a pigment; the neutralizing agent contains a water-soluble amine compound; and the colored fine particle dispersion has a pH value of from 6 to 11, and [2] a process for producing a colored fine particle dispersion containing colored fine particles and a neutralizing agent, said process including the step 1 of subjecting a monomer mixture containing an acid group-containing polymerizable monomer to emulsion polymerization in the presence of a pigment to obtain a colored fine particle dispersion (p); and the step 2 of mixing the colored fine particle dispersion (p) and the neutralizing agent containing a water-soluble amine compound to obtain the colored fine particle dispersion having a pH value of from 6 to 11. The colored fine particle dispersion of the present invention is used in a water-based ink so that the resulting water-based ink is excellent in ejection stability upon evaporation of water from the ink system while maintaining excellent storage stability thereof, and it is possible to obtain printed materials that are excellent in alcohol resistance even when printed on a low-water absorbing printing medium.

The invention concerns:

1. A dispersion of colored fine particles that includes colored fine particles and a neutralizing agent. The colored fine particles are formed by emulsion-polymerizing a monomer mixture that includes an acid group-containing polymerizable monomer, with the polymerization being carried out in the presence of a pigment. The neutralizing agent includes a water-soluble amine compound, and the dispersion has a pH of 6 to 11.

2. A method for preparing such a colored fine particle dispersion. The method includes a first step in which a monomer mixture containing an acid group-containing polymerizable monomer is emulsion-polymerized in the presence of a pigment to produce a colored fine particle dispersion (p). In a second step, the colored fine particle dispersion (p) is combined with a neutralizing agent that includes a water-soluble amine compound, thereby obtaining a colored fine particle dispersion with a pH of 6 to 11.

When incorporated into a water-based ink, the colored fine particle dispersion of this invention allows the ink to retain excellent storage stability while also providing superior ejection stability when water evaporates from the ink system. In addition, even on printing media that absorb little water, the ink can produce printed matter having outstanding resistance to alcohol.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a colored fine particle dispersion that contains colored fine particles and a neutralizing agent. The colored fine particles are obtained by emulsion polymerization of a monomer mixture in the presence of a pigment. The monomer mixture includes an acid group-containing polymerizable monomer, thereby allowing the resulting polymer particles to have acid groups that contribute to dispersion stability and interaction with the neutralizing agent.

The neutralizing agent used in the dispersion contains a water-soluble amine compound. By incorporating this neutralizing agent, the acid groups in the colored fine particles can be at least partially neutralized, improving the stability and usability of the dispersion in aqueous systems. The colored fine particle dispersion is adjusted to have a pH value in the range of 6 to 11, which is suitable for maintaining dispersion stability while also ensuring compatibility with water-based ink formulations.

A process for producing the colored fine particle dispersion includes first preparing the colored fine particles by emulsion polymerization. In this step, the monomer mixture containing the acid group-containing polymerizable monomer is polymerized in the presence of the pigment, so that the pigment is incorporated into or associated with the polymer fine particles. After the emulsion polymerization step, the resulting colored fine particle dispersion is mixed with the neutralizing agent containing the water-soluble amine compound. This produces a stable colored fine particle dispersion having the desired pH and dispersion properties.

The colored fine particle dispersion is particularly useful as a coloring material for water-based ink. When incorporated into such ink, the dispersion provides excellent ejection stability, making it suitable for inkjet recording and other applications requiring reliable discharge from fine nozzles. In addition, the dispersion offers excellent storage stability, allowing the ink to maintain its performance over time. Printed materials formed using the water-based ink exhibit good alcohol resistance, particularly on low-water-absorbing recording media, such as coated paper, films, and other non-porous or poorly absorbent substrates. Thus, the invention provides a colored fine particle dispersion that is highly suitable for producing durable, stable, and high-performance water-based inks.
outputs.L4:
A colored fine particle dispersion suitable for use in water-based inks is prepared by carrying out emulsion polymerization of a monomer mixture in an aqueous medium in the presence of a pigment. The monomer mixture includes, as an essential component, a polymerizable monomer having an acid group, such as a carboxyl group, together with other copolymerizable monomers selected according to the desired film-forming properties, pigment affinity, and ink performance. During polymerization, the pigment becomes stably associated with or encapsulated by the resulting polymer particles, thereby forming colored fine particles dispersed in water.

After the emulsion polymerization step, the dispersion is neutralized with a water-soluble amine compound. The amount of the amine compound is adjusted so that the dispersion has a pH in the range of 6 to 11. By neutralizing the acid groups in the polymer, the colored particles acquire improved dispersibility in the aqueous phase, which suppresses aggregation and sedimentation during storage. The use of a water-soluble amine also helps maintain dispersion stability under conditions in which the water content of the ink changes, such as during prolonged use in an inkjet recording apparatus or exposure to air.

The colored fine particle dispersion obtained in this manner can be formulated into a water-based ink, particularly an inkjet ink. The ink exhibits excellent storage stability, meaning that changes in viscosity, particle size, precipitation, or color density are minimized even after long-term storage. It also provides excellent ejection stability from inkjet nozzles, reducing nozzle clogging, misdirection, or intermittent discharge. These advantages are maintained even when water evaporates from the ink, which is a common cause of increased viscosity and particle aggregation in conventional aqueous pigment inks.

When the ink is applied to a recording medium, especially a medium having low water absorbency such as coated paper, resin-coated paper, plastic film, or other non-porous or semi-non-porous substrates, it forms a printed image with high durability. In particular, the printed matter demonstrates strong resistance to alcohol. This means that the image is less likely to dissolve, smear, peel, or lose optical density when contacted with alcohol-containing liquids. As a result, the ink is useful for producing high-quality printed articles requiring both reliable inkjet performance and resistance to chemical wiping or handling, including labels, packaging materials, films, and coated media.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may seem small and simple, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about specific people, places, things, or ideas. For example, when we say “the book,” we are not talking about any book, but a particular book that the listener or reader can identify.

“The” gives clarity and direction to a sentence. It helps connect ideas and makes communication more precise. Without it, English would often sound incomplete or unclear. Phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” and “the future” show how this tiny word can point to something familiar, unique, or meaningful.

Although “the” is short, it has a powerful role in everyday language. It shows that even the smallest words can have great importance in how we understand and express ideas.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention concerning a colored fine particle dispersion made by emulsion polymerization in the presence of a pigment, neutralized with a water-soluble amine, and useful for water-based inks.
counterfactuals.output: A colored fine particle dispersion is provided which is suitable for use in water-based ink compositions. The dispersion comprises colored polymer fine particles obtained by emulsion polymerization of at least one ethylenically unsaturated monomer in an aqueous medium in the presence of a pigment, whereby the pigment is incorporated in or associated with the polymer particles. The polymer includes an acid-group-containing component, and the resulting dispersion is neutralized with a water-soluble amine to provide stable, finely dispersed colored particles in water. The dispersion exhibits excellent storage stability, dispersibility, color density, and ejection reliability when formulated into an aqueous ink, and is particularly useful for ink-jet recording inks, writing inks, and other water-based coloring compositions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal patent summary for a water-based ink technology that improves ejection stability, storage stability, and alcohol resistance on low-water absorbing media.
counterfactuals.output:
**Patent Summary**

The disclosed invention relates to a water-based ink composition suitable for inkjet recording on low-water absorbing or substantially non-absorbing recording media, such as coated paper, resin films, plastic sheets, and packaging substrates. The ink technology is designed to provide improved ejection stability, long-term storage stability, and enhanced alcohol resistance of printed images.

The water-based ink composition comprises water, a colorant, a resin component, and an organic solvent system selected to control drying behavior, wetting properties, and film formation on low-absorbency media. In certain embodiments, the colorant is a pigment dispersed in the aqueous medium by a polymer dispersant or self-dispersing surface treatment. The resin component may include a water-dispersible resin, such as an acrylic resin, urethane resin, styrene-acrylic resin, polyester resin, or combinations thereof, capable of forming a durable coating film after printing. The ink may further include one or more surfactants for improving wetting and dot spread control, humectants for suppressing nozzle drying, and optional additives such as defoamers, preservatives, pH adjusters, or wax particles.

The composition is formulated so that the ink remains stable during storage, with reduced aggregation, sedimentation, viscosity increase, or phase separation. The solvent and resin balance also contributes to stable inkjet discharge by suppressing nozzle clogging, meniscus instability, and satellite droplet formation, thereby enabling consistent droplet volume and trajectory during continuous or intermittent printing.

When applied to low-water absorbing media, the ink forms a uniform printed layer with strong adhesion and high resistance to alcohol wiping or exposure. The resin component promotes film formation around the colorant, while the solvent system facilitates appropriate leveling and drying without causing excessive bleeding, mottling, or coalescence. As a result, printed images exhibit high optical density, reduced image defects, and improved durability even on difficult substrates where conventional aqueous inks often show poor fixation or insufficient solvent resistance.

Accordingly, the invention provides a water-based ink technology that combines the environmental and handling advantages of aqueous inks with performance characteristics required for printing on non-porous and low-absorbency media, including reliable ejection performance, storage stability, and alcohol-resistant printed matter.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a patent claim-like description of an invention including both a colored fine particle dispersion and a production process with two steps: emulsion polymerization and amine neutralization.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A colored fine particle dispersion** comprising:  
   (a) colored fine particles comprising a polymeric matrix and a colorant retained in or associated with the polymeric matrix; and  
   (b) an aqueous medium in which the colored fine particles are dispersed,  
   wherein the polymeric matrix comprises a polymer obtained from at least one ethylenically unsaturated monomer having an acid group or an acid-forming group, and wherein at least a portion of the acid groups of the polymer are neutralized with an amine compound, thereby providing the colored fine particles with dispersibility in the aqueous medium.

2. **The colored fine particle dispersion according to claim 1**, wherein the colorant comprises at least one pigment, dye, or combination thereof.

3. **The colored fine particle dispersion according to claim 1**, wherein the colored fine particles have an average particle diameter in a submicron range.

4. **The colored fine particle dispersion according to claim 1**, wherein the amine compound is selected from ammonia, a primary amine, a secondary amine, a tertiary amine, an alkanolamine, or a mixture thereof.

5. **A process for producing a colored fine particle dispersion**, the process comprising:  
   (i) **emulsion polymerizing** a monomer composition comprising at least one ethylenically unsaturated monomer and a colorant in an aqueous medium to form colored polymer fine particles having acid groups or acid-forming groups; and  
   (ii) **amine neutralizing** the colored polymer fine particles by adding an amine compound to neutralize at least a portion of the acid groups, thereby obtaining a stable aqueous colored fine particle dispersion.

6. **The process according to claim 5**, wherein the emulsion polymerization is carried out in the presence of a surfactant or a reactive emulsifier.

7. **The process according to claim 5**, wherein the amine neutralization step is performed after completion of the emulsion polymerization.

8. **The process according to claim 5**, wherein the amine neutralization adjusts the dispersion to a pH sufficient to maintain colloidal stability of the colored fine particles.

9. **A colored fine particle dispersion produced by the process according to claim 5.**
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Please create an abstract in patent language for a pigment-containing colored fine particle dispersion produced from an acid-functional monomer mixture, adjusted with a water-soluble amine compound, and suitable for inkjet water-based ink.
counterfactuals.output: An aqueous colored fine particle dispersion is provided, the dispersion comprising pigment-containing polymer fine particles obtained by polymerizing an acid-functional monomer mixture in the presence of a colorant pigment, wherein the acid groups of the resulting polymer are at least partially neutralized with a water-soluble amine compound. The polymer fine particles stably encapsulate or associate with the pigment and are dispersed in an aqueous medium to form a dispersion having excellent storage stability, ejection reliability, and color development. The acid-functional monomer mixture preferably includes an ethylenically unsaturated monomer having a carboxyl group, and the water-soluble amine compound adjusts the neutralization degree and dispersion stability of the fine particles. The colored fine particle dispersion is suitable for use as a colorant component in a water-based inkjet ink, providing improved nozzle discharge performance, reduced aggregation, and high-quality printed images on recording media.
